guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Acute Coronary Syndromes 2021
title: Suspected heart attack in the changing rooms
setting: Football changing rooms. 52M referee walked off the pitch, sitting down, struggling to breathe, pale, sweaty, with severe central chest pain radiating down his arm.
verdictExplanation: Crushing central chest pain with radiation to the arm, shortness of breath, pallor, sweating, and hypotension (77/48). This is suspected myocardial infarction (heart attack). Sick: needs 999.

shared.circulation: Very pale, cold, and clammy skin; weak pulse

history.history: Felt sudden chest tightness while refereeing a match 10 minutes ago, pain spreads to left arm
history.additional: Expresses severe anxiety and a fear of dying

followUp.question: What is the priority medical first aid management for this patient?

options.text: Call 999 immediately, sit him in the 'W' position, administer 300mg chewable aspirin (if not allergic), and monitor closely
Lie him flat on his back with legs raised and encourage him to cough repeatedly
Give him a warm sweet tea and let him rest in the changing room until the match ends
Apply a cold compress to his chest and tell him to walk to his car

followUp.explanation: Suspected heart attack is a critical medical emergency. Call 999 immediately. Sit the patient in the semi-recumbent 'W' position (knees bent, back supported) to reduce cardiac workload. Give 300mg chewable aspirin. Never lay flat (worsens breathing) or allow walking.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999, place in W-position, administer aspirin 300mg if available and no contraindications. Keep him completely at rest.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected STEMI/ACS. Sit in 'W' position, give aspirin 300mg chewable. Administer oxygen if SpO2 <94%. Monitor vitals closely, prepare AED in case of cardiac arrest (VF is a high risk in early MI), and expedite ambulance.
